test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Convex mirrors are fitted on the sides of vehicles because they always give ______.

options.text: a narrower field of the view
an erect and an enlarged image

solution:
The correct answer is __**an erect and diminished image**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Convex mirrors** always produce an erect image irrespective of the distance of the object from the mirror.
 
• The images formed by convex mirrors are always **diminished**, meaning they are smaller than the actual size of the object.
 
• Convex mirrors provide a **wider field of view** compared to plane or concave mirrors, which is crucial for vehicle safety.
 
• Due to these properties, convex mirrors are commonly used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles.
 
• The positioning of convex mirrors helps drivers see a larger area behind them, thereby reducing blind spots.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mirror Terminologies**:

 
 
• **Focal point (F):** The point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• **Principal axis:** The line passing through the center of curvature and the mirror's pole.
 
• **Center of curvature (C):** The center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part.
 
• **Pole (P):** The midpoint of the mirror's surface.
 
 
 
• **Types of Mirrors**:
 
 
• **Plane mirrors:** Produce virtual, erect, and same-sized images as the object.
 
• **Concave mirrors:** Can produce real, inverted images or virtual, erect images depending on the object distance from the mirror.
 
• **Convex mirrors:** Always produce virtual, erect, and diminished images.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors**:
 
 
• Used in vehicle side mirrors for a wider field of view.
 
• Employed in surveillance systems in stores and public places.
 
• Utilized in road safety to give a view of oncoming traffic at blind curves and intersections.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Mirrors**:
 
 
• The nature, size, and orientation of the image formed depend on the type of mirror and the object's distance from the mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors always form virtual images as they diverge light rays.
